peopleAlsoAsk.question: Does heat destroy mRNA?
peopleAlsoAsk.snippet: “An increase in temperature leads to faster biochemical reactions and thus even faster degradation of mRNAs in the cell.” However, there are exceptions. Non-coding RNAs, which are the incapable of protein production, can have a prolonged half-life at high temperatures.
peopleAlsoAsk.title: Heat stress reduces lifetime of mRNA molecules - Biozentrum

peopleAlsoAsk.question: Does RNA degrade at 95 degrees?
peopleAlsoAsk.snippet: It is well known that dsRNA denatures at 95–97 °C [22], followed by degradation of ssRNA [23,24]. Thus, there is a risk of dsRNA destruction during such heat treatment, and the most convenient objects to study this issue are dsRNA fragments of AT-rich genes, for which low thermal stability can be expected.
